newsitem.title: CANADA: Poor Q3 results seen for Canada base metal sector.
newsitem.headline: Poor Q3 results seen for Canada base metal sector.

text.p: Cominco Ltd will likely be the first of a string of Canadian base metal producers expected to post lower earnings in the third quarter, analysts said on Wednesday.

Vancouver-based Cominco said earlier today it expects third quarter earnings to be down from the previous quarter because of lower metal prices, reduced thoughput and grade at its Highland Valley copper mine and scheduled shutdowns at the Sullivan mine and Trail smelter.
"I expect the same thing for all of them (base metal producers)," said industry analyst Tony Hayes at Credifinance.
Since metal prices have been poor this quarter, "...there's very little they can do about it," said Hayes.
"If you don't have the price, you can't have the revenue."

The third quarter has historically produced lower earnings in the mining sector because Canadian companies often schedule shutdowns during the warm summer months, said analyst Bruce Reid of Yorkton Securities.
But this year, the period will hold a double whammy for most companies because of low metal prices.
"It's really copper that is the problem," Reid said. "A lot of companies are going to get slaughtered."
Falconbridge Ltd and Inco Ltd will likely suffer because of their exposure to copper and flat nickel prices, Reid said.
But the two nickel giants will not be hurt as much as Rio Algom Ltd or Noranda Inc because of their relatively greater dependence on copper, he said.
Quarterly earnings will expose the stamina of base metal producers, said analyst Manford Mallory of Research Capital Corp.
Only low-cost producers will be able to report credible profits, Mallory said.
In times of good metals prices, most producers report solid earnings, he explained.
But this quarter, "I think there will be more of a differential in the results."
